raw: {"status": "NO_PLAN", "reasons": ["ST2334 prerequisite requires MA1505, MA1511, MA1521, MA1522, or MA2002. The student must take MA1521 (prerequisite for ST2334 and CS2109S) and MA1522 (prerequisite for ST2334). ST2334 is fixed in Sem 8. MA1521 and MA1522 must be completed before Sem 8. CS2109S requires MA1521 and MA1522 (via the math group) and a data structures course. CS2103T requires CS2030/CS2030S/CS2030DE/CS2030HS and CS2040/CS2040S/CS2040C/CS2040DE/CS2040HS. CS2040S requires CS1231/CS1231S/MA1100/MA1100T. The student has no completed courses. To take CS2103T, one needs CS2030 and CS2040 variants. CS2030 requires CS1010/CS1101S etc. CS2040 requires CS1010/CS1101S etc. The student must take CS1101S (listed as must). CS1101S is offered Sem 1/2. CS2030 and CS2040 variants can be taken in Sem 3/4. CS2103T can be taken in Sem 5/6/7. However, CS2109S requires CS2040 variant and Math. CS3230 requires CS2040 variant and CS1231/MA1100. CS3219 requires CS2103/CS2103T/CS2113. CS2105 requires CS2040 variant. The bottleneck is fitting all prerequisites and corequisites into the limited slots, especially Sem 5 (max 2 modules) and the constraint that CS3230 and ES2660 are not together. With strict prerequisites, it is impossible to schedule all required courses including the heavy Sem 8 load of ST2334 while respecting the Sem 5 limit and mutual exclusions/prerequisites for the earlier courses like CS2103T which needs CS2030 and CS2040. Specifically, CS2103T needs CS2030 and CS2040. CS2030 needs CS1101S. CS2040 needs CS1101S. CS1101S is Sem 1/2. CS2030/CS2040 can be Sem 3/4. CS2103T can be Sem 5/6/7. But Sem 5 is limited to 2 modules. CS2109S, CS3230, CS3219, CS2105 also need to be scheduled. CS3219 needs CS2103T. So CS2103T must be before CS3219. CS3230 needs CS2040. CS2105 needs CS2040. CS2109S needs CS2040 and Math. The number of required courses (12) plus necessary prerequisites (CS1101S, CS2030, CS2040, CS1231/MA1100, MA1521, MA1522) exceeds the capacity given the Sem 5 limit and the fixed Sem 8 slot for ST2334, making a valid plan impossible."}
